Read-only audit of origin/claude/treams-rs-improvements-snetmh at 1f8b6077 (condensed into 8251007). No tests, builds, edits, or remote mutations performed.

Recommended release actions

Priority Action Evidence and confidence
High Reject unsupported spherical Ewald wavenumbers at the shared numerical boundary. Re(k)<0 may silently compute another function. Restrict the Ewald path without removing supported cylindrical or direct-shell inputs. docs/validation/numerical-limits.md:133-150 explicitly records wrong-branch results; python/treams_rs/lattice.py:67-68 says the same. crates/treams-core/src/lattice/mod.rs:437-454 checks finite/nonzero k, then accepts this region. Independent-reference tests deliberately omit negative-real spherical k: tests/lattice/test_lattice.py:928-934. High confidence source finding; known limitation, not a newly reproduced regression.
High Make an explicit release decision about field evaluation’s dependence on length units. Prefer fixing the intermediate scaling; at minimum fail clearly rather than returning NaN for a finite mathematical field. docs/validation/numerical-limits.md:56-57 admits NaN for singular spherical fields at lmax=40, radius 1e-7. crates/treams-core/src/fields.rs:139-159 computes z_l(kr)/r^l; lines 191-208 combine that with dimensional solid harmonics without a finite-result check. The same kernel feeds cached field evaluation (fields.rs:449-475). High confidence documented limitation; no runtime reproduction here.
High Qualify the final integrated source and actual wheel, with numerical optional dependencies installed. Preserve historical evidence as historical. benchmarks/linux-core-qualification.json:5 qualifies 2843a70… (now 7c5ae9d), not this branch or the eventual integration. benchmarks/linux-core-qualification.md:11-20 binds results to September builds. tests/special/test_fractional_legendre.py:17 and the independent qualification-script tests use pytest.importorskip("mpmath"); framework/reference examples also skip absent extras. A green minimal installation is insufficient evidence.
Medium Decide whether gain-media lattice behavior belongs in the supported contract. Narrow the contract or reject the unsupported combinations if the first release promises split-independent outgoing sums. docs/validation/numerical-limits.md:137-150 records discontinuities across real k, split dependence for Im(k)<0, and finite wrong results at certain lattice points. diff.py:361-363 broadly states full sums do not depend on eta. Confirmed contract tension; I have not established a local derivative bug, since branch changes may be discontinuous.

Validation to require after integration

  • Rust physical/reference/gradient suites and full Python suites on supported Python versions, with mpmath, upstream reference packages, and all advertised adapters present.
  • A regression matrix through public scalar/batched lattice calls and diff.lattice_sum for accepted versus rejected wavenumber regions.
  • Field values and physical pullbacks for identical dimensionless geometry expressed in metres, micrometres, and normalized units, including the documented degree-40 case.
  • Installed-wheel numerical/user-workflow checks; record final source and binary identity separately from old benchmark records.

Limits that can remain explicit for a first release

  • Fractional complex Legendre and fractional pi/tau are unimplemented; near-pole/fractional accuracy bounds are documented (numerical-limits.md:20-35).
  • Public Kambe integrals can lose substantial accuracy or overflow outside the validated region; lattice sums use alternate methods in relevant cases (:75-95).
  • Explicit tiny Ewald splits can retain errors up to their 1e-3 loss threshold; automatic splitting is the documented workaround (:208-224).
  • Threshold singularities, bounded high-order/conditioning domains, CPU-only execution, first-order derivatives, and Python 3.12/3.13 are explicit limits. These do not inherently require wider implementations before release.
  • Homogeneous optimized clusters require non-overlapping nonmagnetic spheres in vacuum; general local-T-matrix callers must ensure enclosing surfaces do not overlap (:336-338).

Cleanup/test findings

No TODO, FIXME, todo!, unimplemented!, or xfail matches in the inspected core/Python/tests. Two ignored Rust tests are intentionally invoked by their parent with --ignored (fpenv.rs:571-585, 593, 616); keep them. Explicit Python skips cover unavailable floating-point/fork capabilities and a ufunc dtype case; keep these too. Dependency-based importorskip needs correct release-test environments, not deletion.

This is a targeted source audit of numerical boundaries and evidence, not exhaustive scientific certification of the branch’s 556-file change.

Committed 52e7d08e1e3900e85546669a1cd7c06efc8a913d on release/numerics; worktree clean.

  • Stabilized spherical fields and analytic gradients across length units; removed redundant harmonic cache.
  • Rejected unsupported gain/negative-real spherical Ewald inputs while preserving direct shells and supported cylindrical paths.
  • Verified: 218 Rust tests, 1,229 Python tests, three additional singular-field checks, and all commit hooks passed.
  • Remaining: regenerate combined API docs; final integrated wheel/platform and performance checks belong to root.
  • Author/committer verified. Nothing pushed; no remote changes.
